cruelty.basis: Delmas reposes the corpse for a better-selling photo and plans to shoot the widow's face as she is told she is a widow.

irony.basis: Resistance-hero cover story set against the mistress's apartment, but Delmas's final act of dumping the film is played straight.

ambiguity.basis: Cause of death, the affair and the suppression all settled; only Delmas's laugh at the drain is left unexplained.

fracture.basis: One continuous night, evening of December 23 to the following dawn, in order.

dread.basis: A child face-down in the sea, then days of searching, the hidden luggage, and Alireza's arrival — harm expected continuously after the disappearance.

cruelty.basis: The group pressures Sepideh into lying about the dead woman's willingness to protect themselves; the harm is collective, not staged for us.

irony.basis: The mortuary identification and breakdown are given without any framing distance.

ambiguity.basis: The body is identified but the text never settles whether Elly drowned reaching Arash or walked into the sea.

fracture.basis: Straight chronology from the drive out; the deception is disclosed by later revelation, not by reordering.

the man who wasn t there.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
the man who wasn t there.wikipedia: The Man Who Wasn't There (2001 film)

dread.basis: Blackmail, a beating, a stabbing, two arrests and a death sentence arrive as a continuous descending chain with no interval of safety.

cruelty.basis: Doris hangs herself pregnant, Frank is destroyed, Ed is convicted of the killing he didn't do and executed — misfortune stacked without relief.

irony.basis: He is acquitted of his real killing and condemned for another man's; the lawyer feeds on the defence fund; a UFO appears on death row.

ambiguity.basis: Both murders and both trials are accounted for; only the UFO and Doris's pregnancy stay unexplained.

fracture.basis: Events run in order from the barbershop to the chair; the memoir is written inside that order, not used to reshuffle it.

dread.basis: The stakes are a wife's suspicion and a night of driving; the suicide condition is revealed only at 7am, after the danger has passed.

cruelty.basis: Ewa's manipulation is desperation, and the film lets both parties leave — he to his family, she to her loneliness — unpunished.

irony.basis: The senile aunt asking about homework and the Santa costume are given plainly, not as commentary.

ambiguity.basis: Ewa explains the whole scheme and the wager, but what she does after they part at dawn is left open.

fracture.basis: Christmas Eve through the following morning in unbroken sequence.

dread.basis: Trained projections attack, sedation makes death mean Limbo, and the kicks must sync — sustained peril, but action-register and time-boxed.

cruelty.basis: Mal's suicide and the framing of Cobb are the deepest harm, and they are grieved rather than dwelt on; the rest is dream combat.

irony.basis: Cobb's reconciliation with his part in Mal's death is played fully straight, as is the reunion with his children.

ambiguity.basis: He declines to watch the totem, and Mal's belief that waking life was a dream is never disproved.

fracture.basis: Three nested levels at different time rates run concurrently, plus retrospective Limbo passages, though the order is recoverable.

star wars episode viii the last jedi.title: Star Wars: Episode VIII – The Last Jedi

dread.basis: A fuel-limited chase with the fleet picked off, but broken up by training on Ahch-To and the Canto Bight excursion.

cruelty.basis: Transports are destroyed after DJ's betrayal and the bridge is wiped out, but the film's attention stays with survival and rescue.

irony.basis: Luke burning the library and Yoda's lightning deflate the Jedi legend, yet the broom boy's gaze is offered wholly sincerely.

ambiguity.basis: Snoke dead, Kylo declared Supreme Leader, Luke dead, the Resistance escaped — every strand named and closed.

fracture.basis: Three parallel strands running forward together, cut between; no displacement in time.

dread.basis: Harm is retrospective — deaths already happened; only the radiation illness arriving mid-visit and Iwakichi's unforeseen arson threaten forward.

cruelty.basis: Sustained suffering but every act shown is care: adoption offers, a neighbour's help, new shoes; the one burning is self-inflicted sacrifice.

irony.basis: A teacher visiting graves, orphans and dying pupils, taken entirely at face value; no gap anywhere between what is shown and meant.

ambiguity.basis: Every thread closes: Iwakichi dies, Tarō leaves with the ashes; only Natsue's adoption is left pending.

fracture.basis: One holiday, one direction — a chain of visits in the order she makes them, no displacement.

to live and die in l a.title: To Live and Die in L.A.
to live and die in l a.wikipedia: To Live and Die in L.A. (film)

dread.basis: Stakeout murder in the first minutes, then ambush, prison hit, botched robbery and freeway chase — threat is near-continuous but propulsive.

cruelty.basis: Sexual extortion of a parolee, a man covered in shredded bills and set alight, and a close that hands Ruth's life to the next handler.

irony.basis: The protagonist is shot dead mid-plan and his partner ends up dressed like him repeating his line — the film's own hero-cop framing collapses.

ambiguity.basis: Mechanics fully explained (Grimes, the FBI sting), but whether Ruth set Chance up is asserted by Vukovich and never confirmed.

fracture.basis: Strict forward chronology from the Reagan detail to Ruth's packing.

dread.basis: Vollmer's accident, Lause erased from memory, repeated assassination attempts and threatened commitment — the ground stays unsafe throughout.

cruelty.basis: An identity unit is deleted for stability and Stiller is interrogated and framed, but harm is administrative, not lingered over.

irony.basis: The premise puts its own reality in quotes — 'real people', a 'real world' one level up — so no image is quite what it presents itself as.

ambiguity.basis: Einstein's explanation is delivered and acted on, yet nothing rules out the level above being simulated too; the transfer resolves plot, not status.

fracture.basis: Single forward investigation; the only displacement is moving between simulation levels, not in the telling.

dread.basis: The worst prospects are jet lag, a cold phone call and a departure date; nothing in the text threatens anyone.

cruelty.basis: Harm is limited to a slighted friend and a wounding night with the jazz singer; the film's disposition to both leads is forbearing.

irony.basis: Kelly and the whiskey shoot are mocked from a distance, but Bob and Charlotte are presented without any gap between image and intent.

ambiguity.basis: The whispered line at the final embrace is withheld outright — the one decisive fact the film refuses to supply.

fracture.basis: Consecutive hotel days in order, ending at the airport ride.

dread.basis: The whole body runs on an execution clock — motions denied one after another — plus the Klan reunion beating and Wedge's threat.

cruelty.basis: A bombing that kills twin boys and costs a man his legs, a neighbour murdered in front of the children, and a governor's calculated betrayal.

irony.basis: Reconciliation, remorse and the exposure of a wider conspiracy are all played straight as moral argument.

ambiguity.basis: Wedge is named as bomb-maker and arrested, the family history is fully explained, Adam and Lee reconcile.

fracture.basis: A 1967 prologue, a jump of twenty-nine years, and an inset 1950s murder recovered through Lee's account.

the record of a tenement gentleman.title: The Record of a Tenement Gentleman

dread.basis: The only worry is a boy missing for a day, and Tashiro brings him back; scarcity is background, not threat.

cruelty.basis: O-tane rigged into the errand, abandoning him on the dunes and falsely accusing him over persimmons — petty harm, promptly apologised for.

irony.basis: The closing montage of orphans by the Saigō statue undercuts the happy ending slightly; everything else is taken at face value.

ambiguity.basis: The boy is returned to his father and O-tane's change is stated aloud; only her future adoption and those orphans are left open.

fracture.basis: A week of days told in the order they occur, ending in a coda montage.

dread.basis: Shootout, hitmen, a framing for murder — but threats resolve fast into chases and stunts rather than hanging over the film.

cruelty.basis: A fake knife assassin staged to terrorise the witness, Man shot to frame Ka-Kui, and a lawyer beaten for satisfaction at the close.

irony.basis: The brass parading him as a model officer is a wink, but the heroics themselves are shown without distance.

ambiguity.basis: The mole is named, the data recovered, Chu caught and Salina testifies — nothing outstanding.

fracture.basis: One forward chain from Operation Boar Hunt to the mall arrest.

dread.basis: An order to kill hanging over him from the start, a staged hit-and-run to force his hand, capture and torture — the pressure never lifts.

cruelty.basis: Torture is applied twice, on him and on Véronica, who is abducted purely as leverage and dies of it; the assassination is finally carried out.

irony.basis: A man with no convictions works for terrorists, and the closing report of Véronica's death is 'he learned not to be bitter about it'.

ambiguity.basis: His refusals rest on 'he does not feel like it'; motive is never fixed, and the ending drops him without accounting.

fracture.basis: Forward-moving, but recounted at a retrospective remove ('he says he learned'), compressing events into report.

dread.basis: Calvera's promised return structures a siege, but long stretches go to recruiting, fortifying and courtship.

cruelty.basis: A villager killed in the raid and four of the seven shot dead, but the deaths are given last words and honour rather than dwelt on as harm.

irony.basis: Chris's lie about hidden gold to a dying man is a deliberate gap, but the elder's closing speech states the meaning sincerely.

ambiguity.basis: Calvera dead, Chico stays with Petra, and the moral is spoken by the elder and confirmed by Chris.

fracture.basis: Single forward line from raid to graves.

dread.basis: Constant exposure — Dubois caught photographing, the red-headed guard recognising Devereaux, the airport search, Jarré's staged suicide.

cruelty.basis: Carlotta is tortured into naming Juanita, then embraced and shot by her interrogator; Jarré is murdered and dressed as a suicide.

irony.basis: Espionage procedure and the marital betrayal are both played straight; no distance between what is shown and meant.

ambiguity.basis: The ring is named and exposed, but the text itself supplies two incompatible fates for Granville — suicide, or escape to the Soviet Union.

fracture.basis: Forward chronology across Copenhagen, New York, Cuba, Paris; only the parallel strands displace anything.

dread.basis: Mister's beatings and the rape-threat hang over years of Celie's life, but juke-joint and Shug stretches lift it entirely

cruelty.basis: Fathered children taken, Nettie's attempted rape, decades of hidden letters, Sofia beaten by a mob and jailed into a shell

irony.basis: The curse at the table and the hand-clapping reunion are played straight; no gap between image and intent

ambiguity.basis: Parentage, inheritance, Nettie's fate and Mister's redemption are all explicitly settled before the end

fracture.basis: One forward order; 'years later' ellipses advance but never displace the sequence

dread.basis: Town vanishes from maps, signal dies, a drone circles — a long stretch of unexplained wrongness before the hunt begins

irony.basis: The foreigners' scoring argument and the mayor's gift of old food and tattered books are staged as satire

ambiguity.basis: The siege resolves completely; only 'this is only the beginning' is left hanging

fracture.basis: One order, bar to family home to bar

ambiguity.basis: The perpetrator is never named, Andreas' intent with the axe is stated as unclear, Anna's silence and 'forgiveness' explain nothing

fracture.basis: The narrative runs forward but is repeatedly interrupted by actor-interview footage from outside it

fracture.basis: Boardroom to call to drop to arrest in one forward order

cruelty.basis: Forced nude photographing to check for bruises, misgendering by ID card, the kidnapping and taping of her face

irony.basis: The recital and the run with the dog are offered without any distance

ambiguity.basis: The empty numbered locker is never accounted for, and the visions of Orlando are left unplaced

cruelty.basis: Human sacrifice observed, village children enslaved in the mines, Mola Ram devoured by crocodiles

irony.basis: Invoking Shiva to burn the stones is played wholly straight

ambiguity.basis: Stone returned, children freed, villains dead, embrace — nothing withheld

ambiguity.basis: A prologue 'only loosely related' to the film, episodes dealing 'directly or symbolically', and the balloonist left as figure not fact
